records.context: **Offsets are solved globally, never accumulated.** Chaining microscope image field-to-microscope image field shifts along a row of a 10x10 grid adds every pairwise error together, so the last microscope image field lands tens of pixels out with nothing in the output saying so. Instead every overlapping neighbour pair contributes one equation ``p_j - p_i = d_ij`` and the whole set is solved at once as a weighted least-squares problem over the pair graph (see :func:`solve_positions`). Redundant edges — the diagonal neighbours of a grid, the ``i``/``i+2`` pairs of a heavily-overlapped row — then *cancel* error instead of compounding it, and each microscope image field gets a **residual**: how far its solved position sits from what its own pairs asked for. A large residual is the signal that a microscope image field did not register, and it is written into the table rather than averaged away.
records.label: spacr.align#7
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: **Offsets are solved globally, never accumulated.** Chaining tile-to-tile shifts along a row of a 10x10 grid adds every pairwise error together, so the last tile lands tens of pixels out with nothing in the output saying so. Instead every overlapping neighbour pair contributes one equation ``p_j - p_i = d_ij`` and the whole set is solved at once as a weighted least-squares problem over the pair graph (see :func:`solve_positions`). Redundant edges — the diagonal neighbours of a grid, the ``i``/``i+2`` pairs of a heavily-overlapped row — then *cancel* error instead of compounding it, and each tile gets a **residual**: how far its solved position sits from what its own pairs asked for. A large residual is the signal that a tile did not register, and it is written into the table rather than averaged away.
records.translation: **Hliðranir eru leystar heildrænt, aldrei uppsafnaðar.** Að keðja hliðranir milli flísa eftir röð í 10x10 neti leggur allar paravillur saman, svo síðasta flísin lendir tugum díla frá réttum stað án þess að neitt í úttakinu segi það. Þess í stað leggur hvert skarandi nágrannapar til eina jöfnu ``p_j - p_i = d_ij`` og allt safnið er leyst í einu sem vegið minnstu-kvaðrata-verkefni yfir paranetið (sjá :func:`solve_positions`). Óþarfar brúnir — skánágrannar nets, ``i``/``i+2``-pör raðar með mikilli skörun — *eyða* þá villu í stað þess að magna hana, og hver flís fær **leif**: hve langt leyst staða hennar er frá því sem hennar eigin pör báðu um. Stór leif er merki um að flís hafi ekki skráðst, og hún er skrifuð í töfluna frekar en að vera jöfnuð út.

records.context: **A pair that does not register is reported, not guessed.** Phase correlation over a blank or near-empty overlap returns a confident-looking peak that is pure noise. Every pair is therefore scored by the normalised cross-correlation of the two strips *after* the measured shift is applied; below ``min_confidence`` the pair is dropped, and a microscope image field left with no surviving pair keeps its nominal stage position and is marked ``method='nominal'``. A nominally-placed microscope image field is not the same thing as a registered one and :data:`ALIGN_TABLE` says which is which, per microscope image field.
records.label: spacr.align#8
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: **A pair that does not register is reported, not guessed.** Phase correlation over a blank or near-empty overlap returns a confident-looking peak that is pure noise. Every pair is therefore scored by the normalised cross-correlation of the two strips *after* the measured shift is applied; below ``min_confidence`` the pair is dropped, and a tile left with no surviving pair keeps its nominal stage position and is marked ``method='nominal'``. A nominally-placed tile is not the same thing as a registered one and :data:`ALIGN_TABLE` says which is which, per tile.
records.translation: **Tilkynnt er um par sem skráist ekki, ekki giskað.** Fasafylgni yfir auða eða nær tóma skörun skilar sannfærandi toppi sem er hreint suð. Hvert par er því metið með stöðluðu krossfylgni ræmanna tveggja *eftir* að mældri hliðrun hefur verið beitt; undir ``min_confidence`` er parinu sleppt, og flís sem situr eftir án nokkurs gilds pars heldur nafnstöðu sinni á borðinu og er merkt ``method='nominal'``. Flís sem komið er fyrir á nafnstöðu er ekki það sama og skráð flís og :data:`ALIGN_TABLE` segir hvor er hvor, fyrir hverja flís.

records.translation: Hver brún ``(i, j, dy, dx, w)`` leggur til eina vegna jöfnu ``p_j - p_i = (dy, dx)``; hver flís leggur til eina veika jöfnu ``p_i = nominal_i``. Að lágmarka alla leifina í einu er það sem kemur í veg fyrir að villa safnist upp.

records.context: **Why accumulation fails.** Adding every measured shift to the previous position gives ``p_k = sum(d_0..d_k)`` and carries each measurement error forward. Ten tiles with 0.3 px errors place the last tile 3 px away from its correct position. Least squares distributes errors across *identical input measurements*. A real grid has redundant edges, including the tile below, the tile to the right, and the ``i``/``i+2`` pairs in a heavily overlapped row. Their disagreements can cancel instead of accumulating. The returned per-tile residual records the remaining disagreement.
records.label: spacr.align.solve_positions#2
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: **Why not accumulate.** Walking a row and adding each measured shift to the previous position gives ``p_k = sum(d_0..d_k)``, so every measurement error is carried forward: ten tiles with 0.3 px errors put the last one 3 px out, and nothing in the output says so. Least squares over the *same* measurements distributes the error instead — and because a real grid has redundant edges (the tile below as well as the tile to the right, or the ``i``/``i+2`` pairs of a heavily overlapped row), disagreements cancel rather than compound. The surviving disagreement is the per-tile residual, which is returned.
records.translation: **Hvers vegna ekki að safna upp.** Að ganga eftir línu og leggja hverja mælda hliðrun við fyrri stöðu gefur ``p_k = sum(d_0..d_k)``, svo hver mælivilla berst áfram: tíu flísar með 0.3 px villu setja þá síðustu 3 px frá réttum stað og ekkert í úttakinu segir það. Minnstu kvaðröt yfir *sömu* mælingar dreifa villunni í staðinn — og vegna þess að raunverulegt net hefur umframbrúnir (flísin fyrir neðan jafnt sem flísin til hægri, eða ``i``/``i+2``-pör línu með mikilli skörun) eyðist ósamræmi í stað þess að magnast. Ósamræmið sem eftir stendur er leif hverrar flísar, sem er skilað.

records.context: a row carrying ``png_path`` (or ``path``), or a bare path string, which is accepted as-is and only re-anchored. A row with neither raises :class:`CropError`. Re-anchoring goes through :func:`reanchor_path`, so it is separator-agnostic (a Windows path opened on Linux re-anchors), it takes the LAST ``<folder>`` component rather than the first (an old root that itself contained a ``data`` folder used to produce a path naming a directory), and "already under the root" is a component-wise prefix test rather than a substring one. A path carrying no anchor at all is returned untouched even if it points nowhere on this machine, and the failure surfaces on read.
records.label: spacr.crops.PngCropSource.resolve#1
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: a row carrying ``png_path`` (or ``path``), or a bare path string, which is accepted as-is and only re-anchored. A row with neither raises :class:`CropError`. Re-anchoring goes through :func:`reanchor_path`, so it is separator-agnostic (a Windows path opened on Linux re-anchors), it takes the LAST ``<folder>`` component rather than the first (an old root that itself contained a ``data`` folder used to produce a path naming a directory), and "already under the root" is a component-wise prefix test rather than a substring one. A path carrying no anchor at all is returned untouched even if it points nowhere on this machine, and the failure surfaces on read.
records.translation: lína sem ber ``png_path`` (eða ``path``), eða ber slóðarstrengur, sem er tekinn eins og hann er og aðeins festur aftur. Lína með hvorugt kastar :class:`CropError`. Endurfesting fer í gegnum :func:`reanchor_path`, svo hún er óháð skiltákni (Windows-slóð opnuð á Linux festist aftur), hún tekur SÍÐASTA ``<folder>``-liðinn frekar en þann fyrsta (gömul rót sem sjálf innihélt ``data``-möppu gaf áður slóð sem nefndi möppu), og "already under the root" er forskeytispróf eftir liðum frekar en hlutstrengspróf. Slóð sem ber alls enga festu er skilað ósnertri jafnvel þótt hún vísi hvergi á þessari vél, og villan kemur fram við lestur.

It resolves the file's format (see :func:`crop_format_for_png`), reverses the channel axis when the file's ordering differs from the one asked for -- which today means format 2 only, since formats 1 and 3 are both already in declared order -- and narrows to 8 bit with :func:`narrow_to_uint8`, so a legacy dataset and a new one come back identical and the caller never has to know which it opened.

records.source: The one function every consumer of a crop folder should go through. It resolves the file's format (see :func:`crop_format_for_png`), reverses the channel axis when the file's ordering differs from the one asked for -- which today means format 2 only, since formats 1 and 3 are both already in declared order -- and narrows to 8 bit with :func:`narrow_to_uint8`, so a legacy dataset and a new one come back identical and the caller never has to know which it opened.
records.translation: Eina fallið sem allir notendur myndskurðarmöppu ættu að fara í gegnum. Það ákvarðar snið skrárinnar (sjá :func:`crop_format_for_png`), snýr rásaásnum við þegar röðun skrárinnar er önnur en sú sem beðið var um -- sem í dag á aðeins við um snið 2, því snið 1 og 3 eru bæði þegar í uppgefinni röð -- og þrengir í 8 bita með :func:`narrow_to_uint8`, svo eldra gagnasett og nýtt koma eins til baka og kallandinn þarf aldrei að vita hvort hann opnaði.

records.context: :func:`release_canonical_copy` hands the table back. It removes only rows it has matched, in SQL, against ``foreign_<object>`` — same value in every shared column, NULL in every unshared one — so every deleted row still exists in ``foreign_<object>``; it *un-claims* the table in the same transaction, so no record goes on saying the importer owns a table whose rows it no longer has; and it builds the ``<object>_with_foreign`` view, so their numbers stay one query away. records.context: ``run_import`` copies the imported frame into the canonical ``cell`` / ``nucleus`` / ``pathogen`` table when nothing of anyone else's is there, so that a project built purely by import is readable by every spaCR tool. That copy is a *convenience*, and it stops being one the moment spaCR measures the same project itself: measure appends, so its rows would land in the same table beside theirs, and every per-microplate sample position count downstream would be the sum of two populations with nothing distinguishing them.

records.source: ``run_import`` copies the imported frame into the canonical ``cell`` / ``nucleus`` / ``pathogen`` table when nothing of anyone else's is there, so that a project built purely by import is readable by every spaCR tool. That copy is a *convenience*, and it stops being one the moment spaCR measures the same project itself: measure appends, so its rows would land in the same table beside theirs, and every per-well count downstream would be the sum of two populations with nothing distinguishing them.
records.translation: ``run_import`` afritar innflutta rammann í stöðluðu ``cell`` / ``nucleus`` / ``pathogen``-töfluna þegar ekkert frá öðrum er þar, svo að verkefni sem eingöngu er byggt með innflutningi sé læsilegt öllum verkfærum spaCR. Það afrit er *til þæginda*, og það hættir að vera það um leið og spaCR mælir sama verkefnið sjálft: mæling bætir við, svo línur hennar myndu lenda í sömu töflu við hlið lína þeirra, og hver talning á brunn síðar í ferlinu væri summa tveggja þýða án nokkurs sem greinir þau í sundur.

records.context: **3-D requires a z/xy relationship and will not invent one.** With anisotropic voxels an unspaced volume is not merely in unusual units: a voxel count is not proportional to a physical volume, a distance transform measures a different length along z than along x, and ``major_axis_length`` mixes the two. This mirrors :func:`spacr.zstack.resolve_anisotropy`, which raises rather than defaulting to 1.0 because "isotropic" is a claim about the microscope, not a neutral value. Set ``voxel_size_z_um`` and ``voxel_size_xy_um`` (preferred -- it also gives physical units), or set ``anisotropy`` alone (correct geometry, xy-pixel units).

records.source: **3-D requires a z/xy relationship and will not invent one.** With anisotropic voxels an unspaced volume is not merely in unusual units: a voxel count is not proportional to a physical volume, a distance transform measures a different length along z than along x, and ``major_axis_length`` mixes the two. This mirrors :func:`spacr.zstack.resolve_anisotropy`, which raises rather than defaulting to 1.0 because "isotropic" is a claim about the microscope, not a neutral value. Set ``voxel_size_z_um`` and ``voxel_size_xy_um`` (preferred -- it also gives physical units), or set ``anisotropy`` alone (correct geometry, xy-pixel units).
records.translation: **3-D krefst sambands milli z og xy og býr það ekki til.** Með ósamsætum vókselum er óbilað rúmmál ekki einungis í óvenjulegum einingum: vókselfjöldi er ekki í hlutfalli við efnislegt rúmmál, fjarlægðarvörpun mælir aðra lengd eftir z en eftir x og ``major_axis_length`` blandar þessu tvennu saman. Þetta endurspeglar :func:`spacr.zstack.resolve_anisotropy`, sem kastar villu í stað þess að nota sjálfgefið 1.0 vegna þess að "isotropic" er fullyrðing um smásjána, ekki hlutlaust gildi. Setjið ``voxel_size_z_um`` og ``voxel_size_xy_um`` (æskilegt -- það gefur einnig efnislegar einingar), eða setjið ``anisotropy`` eitt og sér (rétt rúmfræði, einingar í xy-dílum).

records.context: **GUI-only, deliberately.** It passes ``cli_note`` and no ``entry``, so ``spacr-run power`` answers with :data:`APP_CLI_NOTE` instead of "unknown module". The reason is not that the sweep cannot execute headless — it can, and the note names the call — but that its *inputs* are not a settings file. Every other ``spacr-run`` module takes a ``src`` and processes it; this one takes a design, and its output is a curve you read by comparing points on it. A settings.csv that pinned one point of that curve would be a worse interface to :func:`spacr.power_model.scan_parameters` than calling it, which is exactly what the note tells the user to do.

records.source: **GUI-only, deliberately.** It passes ``cli_note`` and no ``entry``, so ``spacr-run power`` answers with :data:`APP_CLI_NOTE` instead of "unknown module". The reason is not that the sweep cannot run headless — it can, and the note names the call — but that its *inputs* are not a settings file. Every other ``spacr-run`` module takes a ``src`` and processes it; this one takes a design, and its output is a curve you read by comparing points on it. A settings.csv that pinned one point of that curve would be a worse interface to :func:`spacr.power_model.scan_parameters` than calling it, which is exactly what the note tells the user to do.
records.translation: **Aðeins í GUI, af ásetningi.** Það sendir ``cli_note`` og ekkert ``entry``, svo ``spacr-run power`` svarar með :data:`APP_CLI_NOTE` í stað "unknown module". Ástæðan er ekki sú að yfirferðin geti ekki keyrt án viðmóts — hún getur það og athugasemdin nefnir kallið — heldur sú að *inntök* hennar eru ekki stillingaskrá. Allar aðrar ``spacr-run``-einingar taka ``src`` og vinna úr því; þessi tekur hönnun og úttak hennar er ferill sem lesinn er með því að bera saman punkta á honum. settings.csv sem festi einn punkt á þeim ferli væri verra viðmót að :func:`spacr.power_model.scan_parameters` en að kalla beint á það, sem er einmitt það sem athugasemdin segir notandanum að gera.

records.context: Timelapse first generates masks for a time series and then links adjacent frames. The costs differ greatly: segmenting twelve frames with Cellpose takes tens of seconds, while relinking *the twelve existing label images* with a new ``timelapse_displacement`` takes milliseconds. The preview separates these stages so a slider change does not rerun segmentation:
records.label: spacr.qt.widgets.timelapse_preview#1
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: The Timelapse module is mask generation over a time series followed by frame-to-frame linking. Those two halves cost wildly different amounts: segmenting twelve frames with Cellpose is tens of seconds, re-linking the *same* twelve label images with a new ``timelapse_displacement`` is milliseconds. A preview that re-segments on every slider move is unusable, so this panel splits them:
records.translation: Timelapse-einingin er grímugerð yfir tímaröð og síðan tenging milli ramma. Þessir tveir helmingar kosta gríðarlega mismikið: að skipta tólf römmum með Cellpose tekur tugi sekúndna, að endurtengja *sömu* tólf merkjamyndirnar með nýju ``timelapse_displacement`` tekur millisekúndur. Forskoðun sem skiptir upp á nýtt við hverja hreyfingu sleða er ónothæf, svo þetta spjald aðskilur þá:

records.context: **The sequence is read lazily.** :class:`FrameSequence` never materialises the whole time series: a directory reads one file at a time, a multi-page TIFF reads one page at a time, and an ``.npy`` stack is memory-mapped and sliced. Only the frames the preview actually shows are touched, and a small LRU keeps the scrubber responsive without pinning the movie in RAM.
records.label: spacr.qt.widgets.timelapse_preview#3
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: **The sequence is read lazily.** :class:`FrameSequence` never materialises the whole time series: a directory reads one file at a time, a multi-page TIFF reads one page at a time, and an ``.npy`` stack is memory-mapped and sliced. Only the frames the preview actually shows are touched, and a small LRU keeps the scrubber responsive without pinning the movie in RAM.
records.translation: **Röðin er lesin letilega.** :class:`FrameSequence` raungerir aldrei alla tímaröðina: mappa les eina skrá í einu, margsíðu-TIFF les eina síðu í einu og ``.npy``-stafla er minnisvarpað og hann sneiddur. Aðeins er snert við römmunum sem forskoðunin sýnir í raun, og lítið LRU heldur skrunsleðanum viðbragðsfljótum án þess að festa myndskeiðið í RAM.

records.context: The module provides three things for a workflow processing session:
records.label: spacr.runctx#1
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: The module provides three things for a pipeline run:
records.translation: Einingin veitir þrennt fyrir keyrslu ferlis:

records.context: **One error policy, honoured at every batch boundary.** ``on_error`` is a tri-state, default ``"stop"``:
records.label: spacr.runctx#4
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: **One error policy, honoured at every batch boundary.** ``on_error`` is a tri-state, default ``"stop"``:
records.translation: **Ein villustefna, virt við hver runumörk.** ``on_error`` hefur þrjár stöður, sjálfgefið ``"stop"``:

records.context: ``stop`` the first failed unit aborts the processing session. The default, because a workflow that quietly drops a third of its plates produces a number that looks exactly like a good one. ``skip`` the unit is recorded — on the :class:`~spacr.errors.RunLedger` *and* as a :class:`SkipRecord` naming the unit, the stage and why — and the processing session carries on. Never a silent drop: :attr:`ErrorPolicy.skips` is what was lost. ``retry`` the unit is attempted :attr:`ErrorPolicy.attempts` times with an exponential backoff, and if the budget runs out it behaves exactly like ``stop``.
records.label: spacr.runctx#5
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: ``stop`` the first failed unit aborts the run. The default, because a pipeline that quietly drops a third of its plates produces a number that looks exactly like a good one. ``skip`` the unit is recorded — on the :class:`~spacr.errors.RunLedger` *and* as a :class:`SkipRecord` naming the unit, the stage and why — and the run carries on. Never a silent drop: :attr:`ErrorPolicy.skips` is what was lost. ``retry`` the unit is attempted :attr:`ErrorPolicy.attempts` times with an exponential backoff, and if the budget runs out it behaves exactly like ``stop``.
records.translation: ``stop`` fyrsta eining sem bregst stöðvar keyrsluna. Sjálfgildið, því ferli sem fellur hljóðlaust út þriðjung plata sinna skilar tölu sem lítur nákvæmlega út eins og góð tala. ``skip`` einingin er skráð — í :class:`~spacr.errors.RunLedger` *og* sem :class:`SkipRecord` sem nefnir eininguna, áfangann og ástæðuna — og keyrslan heldur áfram. Aldrei þögult brottfall: :attr:`ErrorPolicy.skips` er það sem tapaðist. ``retry`` einingin er reynd :attr:`ErrorPolicy.attempts` sinnum með veldisvaxandi biðtíma, og ef kvótinn klárast hegðar hún sér nákvæmlega eins og ``stop``.

records.context: Applied at a *batch boundary* — per laboratory microplate, per microplate sample position, per microscope field of view — wherever the workflow has a unit it can name. Every mode records the failure on the :class:`~spacr.errors.RunLedger` (unless ``record`` is False), so the artifact stamp reports the failure in all three modes; the mode only decides whether the processing session continues.

records.source: Applied at a *batch boundary* — per plate, per well, per field — wherever the pipeline has a unit it can name. Every mode records the failure on the :class:`~spacr.errors.RunLedger` (unless ``record`` is False), so the artifact stamp reports the failure in all three modes; the mode only decides whether the run continues.
records.translation: Beitt við *runumörk* — fyrir hverja plötu, hvern brunn, hvert sjónsvið — hvar sem ferlið hefur einingu sem það getur nefnt. Hver hamur skráir villuna í :class:`~spacr.errors.RunLedger` (nema ``record`` sé False), svo afurðastimpillinn tilkynnir villuna í öllum þremur hömum; hamurinn ákveður aðeins hvort keyrslan heldur áfram.

records.context: **The training basis.** Classify (CV) already had all three: ``dataset_mode`` is ``'metadata'``, ``'annotation'`` or ``'measurement'``, and :mod:`spacr.io` builds the dataset from ``class_metadata``/``metadata_rules``, ``annotation_columns``/``annotation_values`` accordingly. Classify (ML) had two, and chose between them **implicitly**: ``ml.py`` asked whether ``annotation_column`` was ``None``. Nothing said so in the settings panel, so a user who filled in an annotation column silently stopped training on their laboratory microplate controls.

records.translation: **Þjálfunargrunnurinn.** Classify (CV) hafði þegar alla þrjá: ``dataset_mode`` er ``'metadata'``, ``'annotation'`` eða ``'measurement'``, og :mod:`spacr.io` byggir gagnasettið úr ``class_metadata``/``metadata_rules``, ``annotation_columns``/``annotation_values`` í samræmi við það.
